lead: A memory-limit breach is observed at the next loop back edge or the next member call, whichever the program reaches first, and an `$a[] = ...` on its own is neither.
body: The allocator raises `SafepointFlags::MEMORY_LIMIT` at the crossing, so a fixture that grows inside a `while` stops inside it; straight-line growth reaches nothing until `run_helper` asks ahead of a member's body. Put the loop or the member call where you want the breach reported, and expect nothing printed after the crossing.
